title: Why would anyone want multiple spouses?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant open with banter about Chuck's childhood phone calls from an Atlanta swingers club and promote an upcoming Atlanta trivia night. They then discuss polygamy: Warren Jeffs and his legal troubles, definitions of polygamy, polyandry, bigamy, and polyamory, the Nyinba people of Nepal, the Zoe tribe, a Malaysian study on children's attitudes toward polygamy, historical polygamy in China, Vietnam and early Judaism, the biological case for polygyny and Dawkins' selfish gene idea, the social and economic drawbacks, and the history of Mormon polygamy from Joseph Smith and Brigham Young through the 1862-era federal crackdown, Utah statehood, the 1890 manifesto, and Mormon fundamentalists. They close with a monogamy argument, a listener mail request, and a sign-off.

entities.name: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints

segments.title: Opening banter and Atlanta trivia night
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about swinging, Chuck's childhood calls from an Atlanta swingers club, and promote the October trivia night in Atlanta and a related band show.

segments.title: Warren Jeffs and legal troubles
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Warren Jeffs, leader of a fundamentalist Mormon sect, who faces charges in Utah and Texas including allegations involving underage marriages, and note that the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints no longer openly practices polygamy.

segments.title: Defining polygamy and related terms
segments.summary: The hosts define polygamy, polygyny, polyandry, bigamy, and polyamory, and note that most societies historically have been polygamous and that monogamy is rare among mammals.

segments.title: Nyinba fraternal polyandry and other cultures
segments.summary: The hosts describe fraternal polyandry among the Nyinba people, where a woman marries several brothers, and mention the Zoe tribe of the Amazon as an example of multiple spouses.

segments.title: Malaysian study and historical polygamy
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a July study in Malaysia where most children in polygamous households said they would not practice polygamy, and cover polygamy historically in early Judaism, China under Confucianism, and Vietnam after war.

segments.title: Biological case for polygyny and social drawbacks
segments.summary: The hosts explain why polygyny makes biological sense through the selfish gene idea and contrast this with social harms including abuse, male authority, dependence of wives, economic strain, and jealousy.

segments.title: Mormon plural marriage history and federal crackdown
segments.summary: The hosts trace Mormon plural marriage from Joseph Smith Jr. and Brigham Young through the 1856 Republican platform, federal laws against polygamy, Utah's statehood bid, the church's change of doctrine, and the formation of fundamentalist sects.

segments.title: Monogamy argument, listener mail call, and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts give a closing argument for monogamy, request listener experiences with polygamy, point to the website search bar, and sign off with a trivia night joke.
